The indexer turns an interaction history into an entity–relation graph and records the
source chunk for every graph item. Chunks are processed in parallel, but names and types
are resolved across the complete batch before the graph is updated.
Structured extraction and temporal grounding.For each chunk, an LLM emits
typed entity mentions and directed (head,relation,tail) mentions with textual descriptions.
The current type vocabulary is supplied as a soft constraint, allowing the extractor to
introduce a more specific label when no existing type is suitable. Dates, durations, and
temporal phrases are retained inside the corresponding entity or relation description rather
than represented as graph nodes. When a dialogue has a session timestamp, relative phrases
such as "yesterday" or "last week" are converted to absolute dates using that timestamp.
The resolved date is stored in the fact

evidence.excerpt:
ActionRAG combines reconciled graph construction with query-local receiver-normalized
diffusion, pruning, and materialization for long-term agent memory. Across eight hetero-
geneous deterministic MAB columns, it records the highest reported retrieval-based score
on six and an unweighted mean of 55.1. Component ablations indicate that the best con-
figuration combines reconciled, summarized indexing with retrieval-time refinement. Gains
center on test-time learning and conflict resolution where weaker MH-DocQA and Detec-
tiveQA results expose limits for narrative evidence. It also maintains low query cost and
sub-half-second main-evaluation retrieval, while packed context remains nearly constant as
the graph grows. Future work can include better algorithms for graph expansion which are
more robust to hyperparameter values.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The reported gains are measured by ground-truth deterministic benchmark metrics rather than a learned or automated evaluator, so no separate corroboration is required.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are established by deterministic MAB column metrics using objective exact match, substring exact match, and Recall@5 scoring.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The system is shaped by fixed heuristic design choices and pretrained BGE-M3 embeddings; the manuscript reports no iterative optimization of diffusion hyperparameters against the benchmark, and the appendix shows the default configuration is not MCC-optimal.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: The experimental results support the primary claims, showing ActionRAG attains an unweighted average of 55.1 on the deterministic MAB tasks (a 5.4-point margin over HippoRAG-v2) while maintaining low per-query cost. The authors candidly acknowledge and document trade-offs where their method underperforms baselines requiring broader narrative context (such as Detective QA and MH-DocQA).
primary.evaluation_assessment: ActionRAG is evaluated across the eight deterministic evaluation columns of MemoryAgentBench (MAB), covering accurate retrieval, test-time learning, long-range understanding, and conflict resolution using objective exact match, substring match, and Recall@5 metrics. The evaluation includes direct comparisons with strong baselines like HippoRAG-v2, component ablations isolating graph construction and diffusion steps, parameter sensitivity tests, and per-query cost and latency profiling.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The headline evaluation relies directly on standard ground-truth deterministic metrics and pre-established benchmark protocols without learned judge reuse.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Deterministic MAB column metrics consisting of objective exact match, substring exact match, and Recall@5.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Pretrained embeddings (BGE-M3) and fixed heuristic graph diffusion/flux equations parameterized by static depth and decay constants without iterative optimization against the benchmark.

primary.limitations: The manuscript explicitly discusses limitations, including weaker performance on narrative multi-hop tasks relative to full-corpus or agentic iterative search, performance degradation under growing distractor volumes in EventQA, and reliance on fixed heuristic diffusion hyperparameters.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is clearly specified, detailing offline triple extraction, type normalization, tiered mention resolution, and online dual-channel seed retrieval. The query-local graph refinement uses an explicit closed-form linear diffusion operator with receiver normalization, raw-seed protection, and hub-penalized flux for triple materialization, supported by pseudocode and comprehensive hyperparameters.
primary.quality_rationale: The paper provides an adequately scoped, well-formulated, and thoroughly ablated contribution to knowledge graph RAG. The evaluation relies on standardized objective benchmarks with clear comparative baselines and transparently documents both strengths and task-specific weaknesses.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces ActionRAG, an external graph memory architecture that couples a cautious indexing pipeline (label reconciliation, tiered entity resolution, and temporal summarization) with query-local receiver-normalized graph diffusion to refine evidence and materialize missing relational triples for LLM agent memory.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The paper provides an adequately scoped, well-formulated, and thoroughly ablated contribution to knowledge graph RAG. The evaluation relies on standardized objective benchmarks with clear comparative baselines and transparently documents both strengths and task-specific weaknesses.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The manuscript explicitly discusses limitations, including weaker performance on narrative multi-hop tasks relative to full-corpus or agentic iterative search, performance degradation under growing distractor volumes in EventQA, and reliance on fixed heuristic diffusion hyperparameters.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Per-category human-LLM agreement audits with Cohen's kappa from 0.81 to 0.96 and objective benchmark ground-truth state probes corroborate the automated evaluation verdicts.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Tri-judge LLM evaluation (primary gpt-4.1-mini and two gemini-2.5-flash auxiliary judges) measuring end-task question answering accuracy across benchmarks.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Turn-level effective surprisal computed from NLI contradiction scoring and cosine semantic deviation, gated deterministically into update rules parameterized by bounded LLM sub-agent scalars.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding improved handling of belief drift, reduced old-memory pull, and memory scalability with bounded effective memory mass are directly corroborated by empirical results, trajectory analyses, and sensitivity sweeps.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The system is evaluated extensively across multiple established benchmarks (LoCoMo, LongMemEval-S, PersonaMem-v2, AMemGym, LoCoMo-Plus) and a newly introduced drift benchmark (DiMoBench), demonstrating consistent performance gains over modern baselines. Detailed ablation studies isolate the contributions of effective surprisal, confidence weighting, and individual update operators.

primary.limitations: The work explicitly documents limitations including turn-level vs. per-item update routing granularity, the reliance on initial Top-k retrieval to detect update-due events, and its current restriction to English dialogue settings.
primary.method_assessment: PreCoMem provides a clear hybrid execution model combining deterministic closed-form confidence updates and retrieval-entropy reliability weighting with bounded scalar proposals from specialized LLM sub-agents. The memory structure cleanly separates mutable beliefs from an immutable episodic trace cache.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a conceptually grounded, mathematically specified, and thoroughly evaluated framework. The empirical validation is exemplary, combining multi-benchmark testing, human audit validation of automated judges, factorial ablations, and thorough latency/scalability profiling.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces PreCoMem, a long-term memory framework for conversational dialogue agents that models memories as confidence-weighted beliefs updated via a predictive coding-inspired effective surprisal gate routing into maintain, profile (hypothesis buffering), or correct operations.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline gains are measured on external benchmarks with ground-truth exact match, simulator success/error recurrence, and external judge protocols, which are materially independent of the teacher-verified GRPO write signal and the RSI regression sets.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: External benchmark protocols: M3-Bench judged accuracy, LoCoMo Mem0-protocol LLM judge, OpenEQA LLM-Match, EgoLifeQA four-choice exact match, and EMem-Bench simulator success and error recurrence.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: GRPO optimizes memory writes against deterministic contract checks and qwen3.7-max teacher replay of original frames; failure-driven RSI selects rule repairs on a held-out regression set.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported performance metrics directly match the tabular evidence, supporting claims of improved accuracy, lower error recurrence, and enhanced generation efficiency using a 9B model.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The framework is comprehensively evaluated across four established long-horizon question-answering benchmarks (M3-Bench-robot, LoCoMo, OpenEQA EM-EQA, EgoLifeQA) and the interactive EMem-Bench, demonstrating clear improvements over prior systems alongside detailed ablation and efficiency studies.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline performance is corroborated across multiple independent benchmarks using varied external metrics including ground-truth exact match and simulator execution success.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard benchmark test suites evaluated via external LLM judges (Mem0 protocol on LoCoMo, LLM-Match on OpenEQA), exact-match multiple-choice QA (EgoLifeQA), benchmark QA protocols (M3-Bench), and task simulator success/error recurrence (EMem-Bench).
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: GRPO training optimizes memory writes via deterministic rule checks and qwen3.7-max teacher verification against original observation frames, while failure-driven RSI optimizes memory rules on regression validation sets.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly acknowledge limitations including failure modes in joint visual/map alignment, validator-proposer bias, potential degradation under distribution shift, and privacy implications of person-linked memories.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, specifying the six memory layers, a dual-level contract distinguishing interface from content validity, objective functions for RL write-learning, and an algorithmic loop for policy repair and replay.
primary.quality_rationale: The paper presents a substantial, well-formulated architectural contribution to embodied agent memory with sound methodological constraints, strong experimental comparisons on recognized standard benchmarks, and honest discussions of system boundaries.
primary.scoped_contribution: BetaMem introduces a six-layer, evidence-grounded long-term memory framework for embodied agents that combines dual-level contract-based write learning (SFT and GRPO with teacher verification) and failure-driven recursive policy self-improvement under explicit resource budgets.
